readingInstruction: Read Psalm 19:1-6. Paul quotes verse 4 in Romans 10:18. Read these six verses as a picture of creation’s wordless sermon, and think about why Paul says it is not enough.
settingTheScene: Psalm 19 is a psalm of David in two parts. Verses 1 to 6 celebrate God’s revelation in creation, and verses 7 to 14 celebrate his revelation in the law. C. S. Lewis called it among the greatest poems in the Psalter. In Romans 10, Paul has just asked, “Have they not heard?” and answers with verse 4 of this psalm: their voice has gone out to all the earth. Today we read the creation half in light of Romans.
observation: “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims his handiwork” (v. 1).
“Day to day pours out speech, and night to night reveals knowledge” (v. 2).
“There is no speech, nor are there words, whose voice is not heard” (v. 3).
“Their voice goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world” (v. 4).
“In them he has set a tent for the sun” (v. 4).
“Which comes out like a bridegroom leaving his chamber” (v. 5).
“And, like a strong man, runs its course with joy” (v. 5).
“And there is nothing hidden from its heat” (v. 6).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with a grand claim: “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims his handiwork.” Creation is a witness. The verbs, declare, proclaim, pour out speech, reveal knowledge, are all verbs of speaking. Day after day, night after night, creation preaches. The sky is God’s billboard, and its message is his glory.

Yet verse 3 adds a paradox: “There is no speech, nor are there words, whose voice is not heard.” The sermon has no words, and yet its voice goes out through all the earth. The message is universal. This is why Paul says in Romans 1:20 that no one has an excuse: God’s eternal power and divine nature have been clearly perceived in the things that have been made. Look up at the stars and you see something of the majesty of the one who made them.

The second half of this section uses the sun as an example. God has set a tent for the sun, and it comes out “like a bridegroom leaving his chamber, and, like a strong man, runs its course with joy.” Its circuit goes from one end of the heavens to the other, and nothing is hidden from its heat. The sun is a great picture of a creature that obeys its Maker: radiant, joyful, regular. It is also a picture of the reach of God’s revelation.

Paul quotes verse 4 in Romans 10:18, but notice how. He has argued that faith comes from hearing the word of Christ. He asks, “Have they not heard?” and answers, “Indeed they have, for their voice has gone out to all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.” Some interpreters think Paul is using the language of Psalm 19 to describe the reach of the gospel preached by the apostles, as the sun’s light reaches everywhere. Others think he is saying that the witness of creation alone leaves everyone accountable. Either way, the point is that general revelation cannot save. Creation shows God’s glory, but only the gospel shows how sinners can be made right with him. That is why the psalm turns, in verse 7, to the law of the LORD, which is perfect, reviving the soul.

Next time you look at the sky, let it point to its maker. Then open your Bible and learn the rest of the story.
connection: Psalm 8 and Psalm 104 also celebrate creation. Job 38 to 41 is God’s speech from the whirlwind. Isaiah 40:26 invites us to lift up our eyes and see who created these. Romans 1:19-20 and 10:18 draw from this psalm. Acts 14:17 and 17:24-28 speak of God’s witness in nature. Colossians 1:23 speaks of the gospel proclaimed in all creation. John 1:1-5 speaks of the Word through whom all things were made. Revelation 21:23 says the city has no need of sun or moon, for the Lamb is its light.
application:
Go outside today and look at the sky, day or night. Let it declare the glory of God to you.

Thank God for the sun, which rises each day on his command.

Pray for someone who has only creation’s witness and has never heard the gospel.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the speech of the heavens.
Ask him to open your ears to hear it.
Tell him where you have been deaf.
